gameSystem.name: Percentile Horror
gameSystem.description: A 1920s investigation of quiet dread for one investigator. Roll a percentile die under your skill, keep your Sanity and follow a trail of your own choosing to a haunted Kingsport. Original content on an open rules base.

entries.text: A shuttered chandler's shop on the wharf
The old customs house, half empty since the war
A boarding house on Lantern Hill
A fishing cannery that stinks of brine
The cemetery behind the harbor chapel
A bookbinder's loft above the market
A lighthouse nobody has lit for years
A doctor's surgery with the blinds drawn
A cottage at the end of a cliff path
A steepled church with a locked crypt
A tea room that closes at dusk
A cellar under the town hall
A letter from a relative in Kingsport asks you to come at once
An invitation to a party at a house you have never heard of
A newspaper clipping arrives in the mail with no note
A telegram from an old acquaintance: only your name and the word please
Your old professor asks a favor and will not say what it is
An estate in Kingsport has been left to you and must be settled
A notice in the papers lists someone you know as missing
A photograph of your own front door, mailed from Kingsport
A client hires you to find a ledger last seen in the harbor
A dying friend's last letter names a place and a night
Your doctor prescribes sea air, and a particular boarding house
A book you once lent comes back with pages added
A page torn from a diary, dated the night of the storm
A tide table with one night circled in red
A key too old for any lock in town
A photograph with one face scratched out
Wet footprints that end at a bricked-up wall
A ledger of payments to a name nobody admits to knowing
A sketch of a doorway that does not exist on any plan
A tin box of letters tied with fishing line
A map of the coast with new islands drawn in
A phrase scrawled under the stairs, in a hand that is not human
A bottle of salt water that is still warm
A neighbor who remembers a stranger who never left
A fog rolls in against the wind
Every dog in the street falls silent at once
A stranger shows a kindness that feels like a warning
Your lamp burns blue for a moment
Footsteps follow yours and stop when you stop
A hint of dawn comes early and calms you
Your reflection lags a heartbeat behind
Gulls gather on the roof and watch the door
A whisper says your name from the empty room
A bystander offers help and asks for nothing
Salt crusts the windows on the inside
A drowned congregation that still holds its hymns
Something vast and patient behind the cellar wall
A relative who is no longer entirely a relative
A tide-borne thing that wants to be remembered
A chorus of voices from a sealed well
A door that opens on the wrong decade
A shape in the lighthouse that borrows the lamp's light
A swarm of pale things in the crypt
A gentleman in a good coat who casts no shadow
A hunger that has learned to write letters

tags.hint: Someone who calls you or talks to you

tags.label: Mystery
tags.hint: The question your investigation is after

trackers.name: Clues
trackers.hint: At 4 you know enough to face what waits

trackers.name: Dread

sceneTypes.name: Setup
sceneTypes.purpose: Set up your investigator and what draws them to Kingsport.
sceneTypes.tips: Keep it short: a name, a trade and one thing you fear. Roll the tables for ideas, then write each answer in your own words. The facts you fill appear in the Facts panel and come back at the end.

setup.title: Who are you?
setup.tip: First make your investigator in the Characters panel and fill in the sheet, then choose them here; choosing them sets Sanity to Power. Either roll with the dice roller: 3d6 x 5 for Strength, Constitution, Dexterity, Appearance and Power; (2d6 + 6) x 5 for Size, Intelligence and Education; 3d6 x 5 for Luck. Or spend points: about 460 across the eight characteristics, each from 15 to 90. Set Hit points and Magic points from the derived values. Then spread skill points over the skills your trade would use.

setup.title: Who calls you to Kingsport?
setup.tip: Just a name: it becomes an NPC. Roll the Names table if you have no one in mind.

setup.title: What draws you there?
setup.tip: A letter, an invitation, a debt, a rumor. Write it in your own words.

setup.title: Where does the trail start?
setup.tip: A street, a building, a person's door.

setup.title: What is the mystery?
setup.tip: One line you can track, a question to answer before the end. It becomes a Thread.

setup.title: How do you reach Kingsport?
setup.tip: A train, a steamer, a borrowed car. Describe the last mile.

sceneTypes.name: Archive
sceneTypes.purpose: Dig through records, newspapers and old books.
sceneTypes.tips: Say what you hope to find and where you look. A good find is a clue; a bad roll costs a night.

play.title: What do you look up, and where?
Do you find it?
play.tip: Roll Library use. Any success finds a clue; a fumble costs you a night of dread.

play.title: A dead end
play.tip: Nothing useful turns up. Say what you do with the rest of the day.

play.title: What do you find?
play.tip: Roll for ideas, then write the find in your own words.

sceneTypes.name: Interview
sceneTypes.purpose: Talk to a local who knows more than they say.
sceneTypes.tips: Decide what you want from them before you ask. Persuade opens people up; Psychology tells you what they hide.

play.title: Who do you talk to, and what do you want to know?
play.tip: Just a name: it becomes the NPC's name. Use the Names table if you have no one in mind.

play.title: Do they open up?
play.tip: Roll Persuade. Any success gets you an answer; a failure lets you read them instead.

play.title: Can you read what they hide?
play.tip: Roll Psychology. A success shows you where the truth sits; a failure and they clam up.

play.title: What do they tell you?
play.tip: One clear fact, even if it raises more questions.

sceneTypes.name: Site
sceneTypes.purpose: Search a place where something happened.
sceneTypes.tips: Describe one room, one detail at a time. The finds are hard to see: only a hard success turns up a clue, and what you find can break your nerve.

play.title: Where do you go, and how do you get in?
Is anyone else here?
play.tip: Ask it as 50/50 unless the place is clearly watched.

play.title: Do you notice what is wrong?
play.tip: Roll Spot hidden. It needs a hard success: a regular one sees only the obvious.

play.title: You see nothing you can use
play.tip: The place keeps its secret for now.

play.title: What do you find?
play.tip: Roll for ideas, then write the find in your own words.

play.title: What does it hint at?
play.tip: Only when the find is truly disturbing.

play.title: Does it break your nerve?
play.tip: Roll Sanity. A success costs 1 Sanity, a failure 1d6, a fumble 6; the sheet keeps the count.

sceneTypes.name: Night
sceneTypes.tips: Dusk changes the town. Something strange happens, and you decide how you keep your head.

play.title: What happens in the dark?
play.tip: Roll for ideas, then write what happens. If it should shake you, raise the Dread clock yourself.

play.title: Do you slip away unseen?
play.tip: Roll Stealth. A failure raises the dread by one; a fumble raises it by two and a fall or a blow costs 1d6 hit points.

play.title: Do you keep your head?
play.tip: Roll Sanity. A success costs 1 Sanity, a failure 1d6, a fumble 6; the sheet keeps the count.

sceneTypes.name: Confrontation
sceneTypes.purpose: Face what waits at the end of the trail.
sceneTypes.tips: Be brave on the page and honest in the dice. Win by willpower, not by shooting: the horror is not something a pistol solves.

setup.title: Where does it wait?
setup.prompt: The trail began at {fact:place}. Where does it end? Describe the place and the first thing you notice.

play.title: What waits for you?
play.tip: Decide what the clues point to, in your own words.

play.title: Do you hold your ground?
play.tip: Roll Power. It needs a hard success: a regular one is not enough against this, and a miss costs 1d6 hit points.

play.title: It slips your grasp
play.prompt: {fact:horror} is still there. What does it cost you to get away?

play.title: You drive it back
play.prompt: Say how you end it, and what you leave behind in {fact:lair}.

play.title: Does the truth break you?
play.tip: Roll Sanity. A success costs 1 Sanity, a failure 1d10, a fumble 10; the sheet keeps the count.

sceneTypes.name: Epilogue
sceneTypes.purpose: Settle what the night leaves you.
sceneTypes.tips: Look back over the dread you carried and the clues you won.

setup.title: Is the mystery solved?
setup.tip: Close it if you know the truth, even a terrible one. Leave it open if it still haunts you.

setup.title: How shaken are you?
setup.tip: Decided by the dread: above 2 and the nights follow you home.

setup.title: You sleep again
setup.prompt: You write home about what drew you here: {fact:hook}. What do you tell {fact:contact}?

setup.title: The nights follow you
setup.prompt: You leave Kingsport but not the dream. What do you still hear?

flows.name: The Kingsport Mystery
flows.description: A one-shot investigation: something calls you to Kingsport, you dig for the truth, and you face what waits.
flows.introduction:
Solo play means you are the whole table: you describe what happens, roll the dice and make the calls. This guide gives you the questions so you can keep the story moving.

You play one investigator. Something calls you to Kingsport, and you choose what: a letter, an invitation, a debt, a rumor. You search archives, talk to locals, visit a place where something happened and endure the nights. Each step asks you something or tells you what to roll. Steps marked mandatory must be done; the others are suggested and you can skip them. Tables offer inspiration only: roll them for ideas, then write the facts in your own words.

The mystery you name in the prologue becomes a Thread. Threads are the open questions of your story: keep them in view and close them when you have the answer.

To check a skill, roll a percentile die. Equal to or under your skill is a success; a fifth of it is extreme and half of it is hard. A roll of 1 is critical, and 96 or more is a fumble (100 only, if your skill is 50 or more). Watch your Sanity and the Dread clock: when the clock fills, the night closes in.

In the investigation you choose which scene to play next. When you know enough, or the dread is full, the investigation ends and you face what waits.

phases.name: Prologue
phases.description: Create your investigator, name who or what calls you to Kingsport and the mystery you will follow. It is done when you have played the Setup scene.

phases.name: Investigation
phases.description: Dig for the truth in archives, interviews, sites and nights. It ends when you hold 4 clues or the Dread clock is full.

sceneClosing.title: Do you know enough?
sceneClosing.tip: With 4 clues you can face what waits.

sceneClosing.title: Is the dread full?
sceneClosing.tip: At 6/6 the night closes in and you must act.

worldTurn.title: Does the town press closer?
worldTurn.tip: Roll 1d6. On 1 or 2 the dread rises by one.

phases.name: Confrontation
phases.description: Reach the place where it waits, decide what you face, and hold your ground. It is done when the final Sanity check is made.

phases.name: Epilogue
phases.description: Close the mystery and settle what the night leaves you. It is done when you have written how you carry it home.

fields.label: Education

fields.label: Hit points
fields.hint: Constitution plus Size, divided by ten: set your Hit points track to it.

fields.label: Magic points

fields.label: Magic points
